justifications.durability: The rule is pinned from both sides. The new file drives resume_plan through four runs that differ only in what is known of the worker's end and asserts each outcome — the exit record licenses a lift, a pid this host checked dead licenses a lift, unknown liveness is refused with 'liveness unknown' named, and a real live child keeps the message the guard always gave (tests/test_direct_resume_needs_an_observed_death.py:212-269). The live child is started by the test and the dead pid is beyond the kernel's ceiling, so the process table is asked rather than stubbed. Removing the guard reddens 3 of the 4 cases — measured here, not assumed. The 22 repaired fixtures make the existing fixtures state the observation they rest on rather than weakening what they assert.
justifications.evidence: Strong and independently re-derived: the two-arm gate ran the measurement's own population with a separate basetemp per arm under /tmp/gate2 outside any repository, each log carrying revision, tree, measurement cwd, module of record and command (gate-base.log, gate-head.log); the manifest's ids equal the logs' ids; the base tree is byte-identical to an independent export of 2d792b29; and the declared negative control exists with the mutation verbatim on its first line and EXIT=1. Two deductions hold it below 20. The population missed a file that does invoke crew resume through CliRunner — my arm pair shows it adds nothing, but the gap was real and unremarked in the manifest. And the head arm's log labels itself 'c671a521+worktree', so no log ties the 22/395 result to the delivered commit d6dcefb3; the two revisions' production source is identical and the later commit is test-only, which I checked, but the record required that check rather than carrying it.
justifications.fit: Follows the repository's established shape rather than inventing one. The guard reuses the sweep's own helper instead of recomposing the reading, which is the same choice the landed sibling node made when it hoisted _process_reading; the repairs import tests.test_a_live_run_never_reads_dead as liveness, the idiom 11 test modules already use, and the helper they need is defined there (:212). What holds it at 18 is test-module coupling in the new file: _write_exit_record and _pointer are defined locally and 6 other suites import the same helper from the node's own test module, so the node's test file becomes shared fixture surface for unrelated suites — a pattern the plan's sibling nodes already repeat (4 definitions of _write_exit_record in tests/), so it is convention-following rather than novel, but it is coupling all the same.
justifications.goal_fidelity: The plan's follow-up names the defect exactly — the hand-typed door carried only its own live-process guard — and the change closes it at the named function with the named reading, in the named file, plus the tests. The guard is consulted after the launcher's other guards and before anything is written, and its refusal composes with the three-way vocabulary the row already states (alive / process gone / liveness unknown), so a reader of the row and a reader of the refusal see one reading. Docked one point because the same rule's backend-override door is left open by the CLI's early return, and while the plan did not name it, a later reader of this landing could reasonably take 'a hand-typed resume waits for an observed end' to be complete.
justifications.scope_discipline: Exemplary. The three commits touch exactly the 12 declared write paths and nothing else; repaired fixtures are confined to the files the guard reddened; no shared state, index or plan file is written; the reviewed worktree is clean at head with all three commits unpushed for the coordinator to merge.
